name: Imagawa-Matsumoto syndrome
aliases: overgrowth and intellectual disability syndrome, SUZ12 type

clinicalPearls: Caused by heterozygous variants in SUZ12, a core subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) that is required for the complex to trimethylate histone H3 at lysine 27 and silence target genes
Presents as a Weaver-like overgrowth disorder with tall stature, macrocephaly, advanced bone age and intellectual disability
Facial features overlap Weaver syndrome, including a broad forehead, hypertelorism, large ears and a small pointed chin
It completes the PRC2 overgrowth spectrum alongside Weaver syndrome (EZH2) and Cohen-Gibson syndrome (EED), the three sharing a common epigenetic mechanism
Skeletal features may include camptodactyly, joint laxity and other limb anomalies
Because PRC2 loss relaxes silencing of proliferation-related genes, tumour surveillance is considered in line with practice for the wider PRC2 overgrowth group
Diagnosis rests on molecular identification of a pathogenic SUZ12 variant, supported by a recognisable overgrowth episignature where available
reference.pathophysiology: SUZ12 encodes an indispensable structural subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2, the assembly that, through its catalytic partner EZH2, deposits the repressive mark H3K27me3 to keep developmental genes appropriately silenced. Pathogenic SUZ12 variants destabilise the complex and impair its methyltransferase activity, weakening repression of genes that drive growth and proliferation. The consequent loss of transcriptional restraint produces generalised overgrowth, advanced skeletal maturation and disordered neurodevelopment, and because Weaver, Cohen-Gibson and Imagawa-Matsumoto syndromes all disable this single complex, they present with strongly overlapping clinical features.
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing to identify pathogenic SUZ12 variants
DNA methylation episignature analysis where a validated overgrowth signature is available
Bone age radiograph to document advanced skeletal maturation
Serial growth and head circumference charting
Brain MRI if structural anomalies or seizures are suspected
Clinical tumour surveillance consistent with the wider PRC2 overgrowth group
redFlags: Disproportionate or accelerating overgrowth prompting review for a tumour
New abdominal mass or unexplained pain requiring imaging
Rapidly enlarging head circumference or neurological change
Severe hypotonia or feeding difficulty in infancy
reference.prognosis: Data are limited by rarity, but the picture resembles the wider PRC2 overgrowth group, with persistent overgrowth and intellectual disability of variable severity; life expectancy is not clearly reduced without malignancy, and care centres on developmental support, orthopaedic monitoring and tumour vigilance.
pitfalls: Ascribing the overgrowth to Sotos or Weaver syndrome without gene-specific testing across the PRC2 group
Neglecting the tumour surveillance considerations that apply to PRC2-related overgrowth
Overlooking advanced bone age as a diagnostic clue
Assuming normal cognition because overgrowth dominates the clinical picture
references: Nature Reviews — Polycomb repressive complexes in development and disease
management: There is no specific therapy, so centre care on developmental and educational support for the intellectual disability
Monitor growth and head circumference and provide orthopaedic assessment for camptodactyly, joint laxity and other skeletal anomalies
Undertake tumour surveillance in line with practice for the wider PRC2 overgrowth spectrum, given relaxed silencing of proliferation genes
Investigate and manage seizures or structural brain anomalies with neurology and imaging as indicated
Coordinate care through clinical genetics, paediatrics and orthopaedics
Offer genetic counselling for the family regarding this heterozygous SUZ12 disorder
